topic.source_contract: Planning enforcement, lawful-development certificates and appeals

facts.breach: unauthorised development or failure to comply with a condition
facts.guard: enforcement power and record are not automatic proof of current breach or title status
certificate concerns planning lawfulness only and does not replace other consents
submission route is not appeal success
procedural guidance is not a candidate decision
appeal right is not certificate grant or planning permission

scope_guards: Enforcement action is discretionary and proposal-specific.
An allegation or complaint is not proof of a breach.
An enforcement notice must be matched to its exact land, breach, requirements and effective status.
A lawful-development certificate concerns planning lawfulness, not building regulations, listed-building consent, licences or permits.
Existing and proposed certificates remain distinct.
An appeal submission or procedural guide is not an appeal outcome.
Planning-history entries are not HMLR title or current use evidence by themselves.
No score or promotion is written without exact site, notice, certificate, appeal and current planning evidence.
